settings.title: Settings
settings.inviteBody: Share this code with a parent so they can see how you are doing.
settings.inviteParentBody: Send a link to a parent, an older brother or sister, or a tutor — anyone who helps you. They can only look; they cannot change anything.
settings.inviteParentHow: Read it out to them, or send it on WhatsApp. In Saathi they tap “I have a parent code” and enter it.
settings.inviteParentExpiry: This code works for {hours, plural, one {# more hour} other {# more hours}}.
settings.inviteParentSees: They will see: lessons you finished, which topics you are getting, your streak and your badges.
settings.inviteParentPrivate: They will not see the questions you asked Saathi. That stays yours.
settings.inviteParentShareMessage: I am learning maths on Saathi. You can see how I am doing — open {url} and enter my code {code}
settings.shareLinkMessage: I am learning maths on Saathi. You can see how I am doing here — no sign-up needed: {url}
settings.shareLinkViews: Opened {count, plural, one {# time} other {# times}} so far.
settings.inviteParentCodeWhy: A code lets them make their own Saathi account and sign in whenever they like. Useful for a tutor, or if more than one of you uses Saathi.
settings.inviteParentCodeToggle: Or give them a code for their own account

parent.claimIsLearner: This account is a learner's. Ask a parent to use their own.

parent.lessonsMeaning: A lesson is a short reading with an example. Each one takes about ten minutes.
parent.practiceMeaning: Practice questions are how the topic sticks. Around five a day is a good rhythm.
parent.streakMeaning: Days in a row with some learning done. Streaks are about the habit, not the score.
parent.milestonesMeaning: Badges are earned automatically for real progress. They are worth saying out loud at home.
parent.conceptsMeaning: “Mastered” means they are getting it right consistently. “Keep practising” is not a fail — it is simply the next thing to work on.
parent.helpFocus: If you have ten minutes together, {concept} is the one worth sitting with. You do not need to teach it — ask them to explain it to you, and see where they get stuck.
parent.helpAllWell: Nothing needs fixing this week. Ask them to show you something they worked out — explaining it back is how it sticks.
parent.helpEncourage: Noticing out loud that they showed up is worth more than checking the answers. That is the part only you can do.
parent.linkIntro: This is a read-only view. You cannot change anything here, and it updates as they learn.
parent.linkRevoked: This link is no longer active.
parent.linkRevokedHelp: Ask your child to open Saathi, go to Settings, and share a new one.

forParents.title: For parents
forParents.intro: Saathi is a maths tutor for Classes 6 to 8, following the NCERT syllabus. Your child uses it to learn; you get a simple weekly picture of how they are doing.
forParents.stepsTitle: How to connect to your child
forParents.step1: Your child opens Saathi, goes to Settings, and taps “Invite a parent”. A 6-character code appears on their screen.
forParents.step2: They read it out to you, or send it on WhatsApp. The code works for 3 days.
forParents.step3: You create your own Saathi account here — your email, your password. It is separate from your child's.
forParents.step4: You enter the code once. From then on you go straight to their summary whenever you sign in.
forParents.sees1: How many lessons and practice questions they finished this week
forParents.sees2: Which topics they have got, and which need more practice
forParents.sees3: Their day streak, so you know if they are keeping the habit
forParents.sees4: Badges they earned — the moments worth celebrating at home
forParents.private1: The questions they asked the Saathi tutor. That conversation is theirs alone — it is where a learner admits they are stuck.
forParents.readOnly: Your view is read-only. There is nothing you can change, undo or delete — you cannot affect their learning by tapping anything.
forParents.noCodeBody: Ask your child to open Saathi, go to Settings, and tap “Invite a parent”. It takes them one tap.
forParents.sharedPhoneBody: That works. Both accounts can live on the same phone — sign out from Settings to swap between your child's view and yours.
